questions: Do the rapid eye movements occur in both eyes at the same time?
Do they consist only of rapid back-and-forth movements, without a slower return movement?
Do the bursts occur while you remain fully awake and aware?
Can you stop the eye movements by closing your eyes?
Have you had any double vision during or between the episodes?
Have you had vertigo, severe dizziness, or a spinning sensation?
Have you had new difficulty walking, loss of balance, or problems coordinating your movements?
Have you had jerking movements of your limbs, trunk, or face?
Have you had weakness, numbness, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or facial drooping?
Have you had a new severe headache, fever, or neck stiffness?
Have you recently had an infection or flu-like illness?
Have you started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication or recreational drug before these episodes began?
Have you ever had seizures or episodes of loss of awareness?
Do you have, or have you recently been diagnosed with, cancer?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Postinfectious immune-mediated ocular flutter–cerebellar ataxia syndrome (a limited opsoclonus–myoclonus-spectrum disorder), with no specific infectious agent identified

Alternative: Paraneoplastic opsoclonus–ataxia syndrome

Alternative: Seronegative autoimmune cerebellitis

Alternative: Anti-GAD65–associated autoimmune cerebellar ataxia
